cohort: The study included 325,309 singleton pregnancies delivered via cesarean section under either general or neuraxial anesthesia, after excluding twins, children with congenital anomalies or diseases, and those with missing data.
finding: Initially, general anesthesia for cesarean delivery was associated with a higher risk of developmental disorders within 2-4 years post-birth, but this association was no longer present after accounting for Apgar scores, suggesting no direct relationship between GA-related neurotoxicity and subsequent developmental disorders.
mod_finding: The study investigated the impact of the mode of anesthesia during cesarean birth on developmental disorders, concluding that any observed association between general anesthesia and developmental disorders was mediated through poorer Apgar scores rather than a direct neurotoxic effect.
